My hand: Basri's Acolyte (2WW), Cemetery Recruitment (1B), Ghoulraiser (1BB), Impeccable Timing (1W).

I have 5 mana (1W + 4B). I still can't cast Basri's Acolyte (need 2WW). 

Options:
- Ghoulraiser (1BB) for a 2/2 body - still no zombies in graveyard
- Cemetery Recruitment (1B) to get back Felidar Cub - meh, but it's another body

I should deploy Ghoulraiser for a 2/2 body. Even though there are no zombies to return, it adds pressure. Then I'll still have 2 mana open (1W + 1B) for Impeccable Timing if Steel-Plume Marshal attacks.

llmEvents.reasoning:
Wait, Ghoulraiser is showing as 3/2! It should be 2/2 base... Oh wait, Liliana's Devotee gives Zombies +1/+0! Ghoulraiser IS a Zombie! So it's 3/2. Nice synergy!

Now for attacks. Opponent has Steel-Plume Marshal (3/3, sick) and 1 untapped Plains. They could have a combat trick. But I have Impeccable Timing ready (1W - 3 damage to attacking/blocking creature). Wait, Impeccable Timing only hits attacking or blocking creatures, so it would work if they block.

Ghoulraiser is sick. I can attack with Liliana's Devotee (2/3), Ingenious Leonin (4/4), and Liliana's Elite (3/2). Opponent has Steel-Plume Marshal that could block - but it has summoning sickness so it CAN block.

If Marshal blocks my 4/4 Leonin, it dies (4 damage vs 3 toughness) and deals 3 back (Leonin survives). If it blocks Elite (3/2), both die (3 vs 3, and 3 vs 2). If it blocks Devotee (2/3), neither dies (2 vs 3, 3 vs 3).

Best to attack with all three. If opponent blocks Leonin, we trade favorably. If they block Elite, they trade 1 for 1. If they don't block, we deal 2+4+3 = 9 damage, putting them to 4!

annotations.description: Playing Swamp instead of Plains when holding 3 Swamps and only 1 Plains. The singleton Plains should be played first to ensure white mana availability for Felidar Cub on curve and to avoid risk of missing white mana if something goes wrong. With 3 Swamps in hand, black mana is well-covered for future turns.
annotations.betterLine: Play Plains first, saving the abundant Swamps for later turns. This ensures white mana is available for the curve play (Felidar Cub) and preserves flexibility.

annotations.description: Casting Concordia Pegasus instead of Naga Vitalist when the hand is loaded with expensive spells (Falconer Adept at 4, Enlarge at 5, Steel-Plume Marshal at 5). Naga Vitalist would enable casting Falconer Adept on turn 4 (3 lands + Vitalist = 4 mana), while without it, Falconer Adept can't come down until turn 5. The one-turn acceleration is very significant for this hand's curve.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Naga Vitalist for {1}{G} to ramp into turn 4 Falconer Adept and accelerate toward the 5-mana spells in hand

annotations.description: Blocked a 2/2 Felidar Cub with Naga Vitalist (1/2), which will die in combat. At 20 life, taking 2 damage is trivial, but losing the mana dork significantly slows down casting expensive spells like Steel-Plume Marshal (3WW), Enlarge (3GG), and Falconer Adept (3W). The Vitalist was critical for ramping to 5+ mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Felidar Cub with Naga Vitalist, trading the mana dork for nothing (Cub survives as a 2/2 vs 1/2 blocker).
annotations.betterLine: Don't block. Take 2 damage (going to 18) and preserve the Naga Vitalist to accelerate into Steel-Plume Marshal or Falconer Adept next turn.

annotations.description: Cast Aerial Assault before playing the Forest land. While the end result is the same this turn (no meaningful use for the 4th mana), proper sequencing dictates playing lands before spells to maximize available mana and keep options open.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Aerial Assault on Felidar Cub before playing Forest
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest first, then cast Aerial Assault on Felidar Cub. This leaves 1 mana available after the spell resolves, which is better than 0 mana available during resolution.

annotations.description: With 5 mana available (1W + 4B), Opus Trash could cast both Ghoulraiser (1BB = 3 mana) and Liliana's Elite (2B = 2 mana) in the same turn, deploying two creatures instead of one. Both are Zombies that benefit from Liliana's Devotee's +1/+0 buff. Ghoulraiser would be a 3/2 and Elite would be a 3/2 (1 creature in graveyard + Devotee buff). Two bodies are much better than the single 4/4 Ingenious Leonin, especially with zombie synergies, better blocking coverage against Falconer Adept's flying tokens, and better targets for Basri's Acolyte's +1/+1 counters next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Ingenious Leonin (4W), using all 5 mana for a single 4/4 creature with no synergy.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Ghoulraiser (1BB) and Liliana's Elite (2B) to deploy two Zombie creatures that synergize with Liliana's Devotee, creating a wider board and better board presence.

annotations.description: Used Pounce to have Falconer Adept (2/3) fight Ingenious Leonin (4/4). Falconer Adept dies and Leonin survives at 4/2. This throws away their best creature and a removal spell without killing anything. Falconer Adept could have attacked this turn (generating a bird token) and next turn could have been Enlarged to 9/10 trample for a massive attack. The Leonin was summoning sick and couldn't attack yet.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Pounce targeting Falconer Adept fighting Ingenious Leonin, losing Falconer Adept and only dealing 2 damage to the 4/4 Leonin.
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Heath, then attack with Falconer Adept (creating a 1/1 flying bird token). Save Pounce for a favorable fight later, potentially combining with Enlarge to kill the Leonin while keeping the attacker alive.

annotations.description: Player attempted to block three attackers with a single Steel-Plume Marshal, which is not legal in standard Magic rules. The optimal block would be on Liliana's Elite (3/2), where Steel-Plume Marshal (3/3) would kill the Elite and survive at 3/1, saving 3 damage while preserving the Marshal for the powerful Enlarge combo next turn (10/10 flying trampler).
annotations.actionTaken: Attempted to assign Steel-Plume Marshal to block all three attacking creatures simultaneously.
annotations.betterLine: Block only Liliana's Elite with Steel-Plume Marshal. Marshal's 3 power kills Elite's 2 toughness, Marshal survives, and you take only 6 damage (going to 7) while keeping your key flying threat alive for the Enlarge kill next turn.

annotations.description: Cast Enlarge targeting the opponent's Ghoulraiser instead of their own Steel-Plume Marshal. All opponent creatures are tapped, so a 10/10 flying trampler Steel-Plume Marshal would have dealt 10 unblockable damage (18→8). Instead, Enlarge on an opponent's tapped creature accomplishes absolutely nothing — just wastes the card.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Enlarge targeting opponent's Ghoulraiser (a tapped enemy creature), giving it +7/+7 and trample until end of turn for no benefit.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Enlarge on Steel-Plume Marshal, making it a 10/10 flying trampler, then attack for 10 unblocked damage since all opponent creatures are tapped.
